answer: A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, as the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The inlet multiplier is published, charged in haven, and mesa lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 12 for each account already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 1132 identities would post 1403 proofs and burn roughly 11 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
